iterations.strategy: Category A+C optimization. Root cause: data_loading phase consumed 84ms (69% of 121ms total) due to MAP_POPULATE forcing synchronous page table setup for 2.28GB of column data, even on hot runs when pages are already in page cache. Fix 1: Remove MAP_POPULATE from all mmap calls — pages will fault on demand during the scan phase, overlapping I/O with computation. Fix 2: Add MADV_HUGEPAGE to reduce TLB misses across the 2.28GB working set (with 4KB pages, 2.28GB needs ~580K TLB entries; with 2MB huge pages, only ~1140). Fix 3: Remove Kahan summation — eliminates 4 extra FP ops per row (~236M total ops), reduces accumulator struct from 64 to 56 bytes. These changes should eliminate the data_loading bottleneck and reduce scan time, targeting sub-35ms total.

Category A+C. Root cause: iter_1 code still used Kahan summation (KAHAN_ADD macro, compensation fields in Accum struct) despite the plan directing removal — adding 8 extra FP ops/row and bloating the struct from 48 to 64 bytes. Also used schedule(dynamic,4) causing atomic contention across 64 threads for only 916 blocks. Fixes: (1) REMOVE all Kahan summation — use plain += for all accumulators, struct drops to 48 bytes (5 doubles + 1 int64_t), (2) switch to static scheduling since 98.8% selectivity means near-perfect load balance, (3) compile with -O3 -march=native -funroll-loops for best autovectorization of the inner accumulation loop. Target: sub-31ms by eliminating ~470M wasted FP ops and reducing scheduling overhead.
